identification.summary: Long-running cyber-espionage actor tracked as Inception Framework (Blue Coat, Symantec, Palo Alto Unit 42) and Cloud Atlas (Kaspersky, Check Point). It is known for spear-phishing with weaponized Office documents, layered script-based malware and cloud-service command and control [S1][S5][S10]. In its 2014 reporting Kaspersky called the campaign almost certainly an update of the Red October malware platform [S5]. Since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, reporting shows its targeting has narrowed to Russia, Belarus and contested areas of Ukraine and Moldova [S2]. Kaspersky reported continued activity against Russian and Belarusian government and diplomatic entities into early 2026 [S9].
identification.firstObserved: Active since at least May 2014 according to Symantec, as reported by Security Affairs [S6]. Unit 42 also says the group has been active since at least 2014 [S1]. Kaspersky links it to the Red October operation, which Kaspersky discovered earlier [S5].
identification.notes: Microsoft has no published name for this actor: the MSTIC naming map retrieved for this research has no entry for Cloud Atlas, Inception or its other aliases. Alias set per Brandefense: Inception Framework, Blue Odin, Cloud Atlas, Clean Ursa, ATK116, G0100, OXYGEN [S10]. The MITRE group is G0100 [S11]. The Red October link is Kaspersky's assessment and does not establish a shared operator by itself [S5]. Sources disagree on who coined 'Inception Framework' (Blue Coat or Symantec) [S10].

attribution.confidence: Unattributed in the open sources gathered. Coverage of F.A.C.C.T.'s December 2023 reporting states that it is not clear which country sponsors the group [S7]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: The vendor reporting describes tradecraft and targeting but does not name a sponsoring state [S1][S2][S7]. Targeting has focused heavily on Russia and Belarus: more than 80% of 2024 VBCloud targets were in Russia [S3] [S2].

objectives: Strategic espionage against government, diplomatic and strategic-industry targets. Its focus has shifted to Russia, Belarus and Russia-controlled or contested territories since 2022 [S2][S5][S9]. Its tooling is built for reconnaissance, file theft and long-term persistence [S1][S3][S9].

sectors: Government organizations in Europe, Russia and Central Asia (2017-2018) [S1]
regions: Russia-annexed areas of Ukraine (Crimea, Luhansk, Donetsk) and Transnistria (Moldova) [S2]
Smaller 2024 victim sets in Canada, Moldova, Israel, Kyrgyzstan, Turkey and Vietnam [S3]
targeting.notes: In 2014 Blue Coat observed targeting of a Russian financial firm and of oil and diplomatic organizations in Paraguay, Romania and Turkey [S5]. After February 2022 its targeting narrowed to Russia, Belarus and conflict areas in Ukraine and Moldova [S2]. In 2023 its lures referred to postcards for Russian soldiers and to changes in military reserve law [S7].

capabilities.summary: Initial access is spear-phishing with Office documents that use remote-template injection and exploit Equation Editor flaws CVE-2017-11882 and CVE-2018-0802 [S1][S2][S3][S4][S7]. In 2014 it ran a multi-platform framework covering Windows plus Android, iOS, BlackBerry and Windows Phone. It used CloudMe WebDAV storage for command and control, and its mobile malware was disguised as a fake WhatsApp update [S5]. In 2018 Unit 42 documented the POWERSHOWER PowerShell reconnaissance/validator backdoor [S1]. In 2019 Kaspersky described a polymorphic HTA and VBS implant (VBShower) placed ahead of PowerShower and an unchanged second-stage backdoor [S4]. In 2024 Kaspersky documented the VBCloud file stealer, delivered with VBShower and PowerShower [S3]. Kaspersky's 2025-2026 reporting covers updated VBShower, VBCloud, PowerShower and CloudAtlas backdoors [S8]. It also covers a new PowerCloud tool that sends data to Google Sheets, LNK-in-ZIP delivery, and ReverseSocks, SSH and Tor for persistence (per secondary summaries) [S9]. To hide its origin, the group chained hijacked UPnP-exposed home routers as proxies; Symantec first observed this and Akamai later named it UPnProxy [S6].

campaigns.name: Inception Framework / Cloud Atlas disclosure
campaigns.summary: Blue Coat and Kaspersky disclosed a multi-platform espionage framework that used CloudMe WebDAV command and control against diplomatic, oil and financial targets. Kaspersky linked it to Red October.

campaigns.name: UPnP router proxy chaining
campaigns.summary: Symantec reported that the group hid behind chains of hijacked UPnP routers. Akamai's April 2018 UPnProxy research expanded on the technique.

campaigns.name: POWERSHOWER campaign against Europe
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 observed CVE-2017-11882 documents dropping the new POWERSHOWER backdoor, with reconnaissance and payload delivery in a single document.

campaigns.name: Polymorphic infection chain (VBShower)
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky reported a new chain using a polymorphic HTA and VBS implant ahead of PowerShower.

campaigns.name: Wartime targeting of Russia and Belarus
campaigns.summary: Check Point reported template-injection phishing against Russia, Belarus, annexed Ukrainian territories and Transnistria.

campaigns.name: Military-themed lures against Russian organizations
campaigns.summary: F.A.C.C.T. reported averted attacks on a Russian agro-industrial enterprise and a state-owned research company. The lures exploited CVE-2017-11882.

campaigns.name: VBCloud campaign
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky documented the VBCloud stealer used against several dozen users in 2024, more than 80% of them in Russia.

campaigns.name: H1 2025 tooling updates
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky described updated VBShower, VBCloud, PowerShower and CloudAtlas backdoors.

campaigns.name: H2 2025 to early 2026 activity (PowerCloud)
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky reported continued targeting of government and diplomatic entities in Russia and Belarus, including a new PowerCloud tool.

diamond.adversary: Unattributed espionage operator; the sponsoring state is unclear [S7]. Kaspersky assesses continuity with Red October [S5].
diamond.capability: Office exploits (CVE-2017-11882, CVE-2018-0802), template injection, and the PowerShower, VBShower, VBCloud, PowerCloud and CloudAtlas backdoors. Mobile implants were used in 2014 [S1][S3][S4][S5][S8][S9].
diamond.infrastructure: Cloud storage and web services for command and control: CloudMe WebDAV in 2014 [S5] and Google Sheets for PowerCloud [S9]. Hijacked UPnP home routers served as proxy chains [S6].
diamond.victim: Government, diplomatic, energy, financial, agro-industrial and research organizations, now concentrated in Russia and Belarus [S2][S3][S5][S7][S9].
diamond.socioPolitical: After 2022 the group focuses on Russia, its ally Belarus, and Russia-controlled territories, which is consistent with intelligence interest in the war in Ukraine [S2].
diamond.technology: Unpatched Microsoft Office Equation Editor, trusted cloud SaaS platforms used to blend command-and-control traffic, and consumer routers exposing UPnP [S1][S5][S6][S9].

gaps: No sponsoring state is identified in open sources [S7]. The actor record's country field (RU) is unsupported by the cited sources and conflicts with the actor's heavy targeting of Russia; it needs review.
Microsoft has no published name or mapping for this actor.
Primary documents could not be opened: Securelist (Kaspersky), Check Point Research, The Record and Symantec pages failed to load. Details come from search excerpts and secondary coverage.
Publication dates for the two Kaspersky 2025-2026 Securelist reports (S8, S9) come from secondary timeline entries and are approximate.

Positive Technologies' 'Cloud Atlas: Sheet Happens' report on a campaign against Russian and Belarusian government employees (from late October 2024, using Yandex Disk) was seen only in search snippets and could not be dated; it is not cited.
Scale of the router hijacking is unresolved: Akamai's count is about 65,000 devices, while other coverage gives figures in the hundreds of thousands.
The relationship to the Red October operators is Kaspersky's assessment; no independent confirmation was found.
Who coined the name 'Inception Framework' (Blue Coat or Symantec) is disputed [S10].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (environment): The relevant terrain is diplomatic and government networks of Russia, Belarus and contested Eastern European territories, plus third-country embassies and energy firms. The cloud SaaS platforms (WebDAV storage, Google Sheets) and consumer routers the actor uses as infrastructure are also part of it [S2][S5][S6][S9]. STEP 2 (effects): Reliance on legitimate cloud services and residential router proxies weakens IP-reputation blocking and complicates attribution of its traffic [S5][S6]. STEP 3 (threat model): Spear-phish with a template-injection or Equation Editor exploit, then a polymorphic HTA/VBS validator (VBShower), PowerShower reconnaissance, a second-stage backdoor or stealer (VBCloud, CloudAtlas), and exfiltration to cloud storage [S1][S3][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued selective collection against Russian and Belarusian government and diplomatic targets using updated script implants [S9]. MDCOA, which is speculative, is renewed targeting of Western or partner embassies and energy organizations, as in 2014 [S5], using the same chain. Candidate indicators: Office documents fetching remote RTF templates; EQNEDT32.EXE spawning processes; mshta or regsvr32 running scripts from user directories; unexpected WebDAV or Google Sheets API traffic from endpoints; PowerShell reconnaissance scripts that delete themselves [S1][S3][S5][S9].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: the group mostly targets Russia and Belarus, so its tooling updates are a useful collection signal on intelligence competition in the region. They are also an early warning if targeting widens back to partner diplomatic or energy entities [S2][S5][S9]. (2) Authorities: the sponsor is unknown, so treat the actor as a third-party espionage threat and attribute effects cautiously; routers used as proxies belong to uninvolved residential users [S6][S7]. (3) Mission assurance: patching or disabling Equation Editor and blocking remote template retrieval cuts off the group's long-running initial access vector [S1][S3]. (4) Coordination: cloud-provider takedowns (such as CloudMe's 2014 account removals) and ISP/router remediation require coordination with commercial partners [S5][S6].
